Kuvitus: tähtitaivas, jolla hehkuu kymme: Illustration: a starry sky where about ten galaxies of different sizes glow, large ones near and small ones far away. Below, on a hill, is an observatory, and a telescope points to the sky through the slit of its dome.
Kaavakuva, aallonpituusasteikko mittakaa: Schematic, wavelength scale to scale 400–720 nanometres. The upper colour band is the spectrum of light that has passed through hydrogen gas in the laboratory: it has four dark absorption lines at wavelengths 410, 434, 486 and 656 nanometres. The lower colour band is the spectrum of the light of a distant galaxy, where the same four lines have shifted to longer wavelengths, that is, towards red, each by 5.0 percent of its own wavelength. Dashed lines connect the corresponding lines. The shift of the red line from 656.3 nanometres to 689.1 nanometres is marked with an arrow Δλ. Below it reads z = Δλ / λ0 = 0.050.
Kaavakuva, etäisyydet mittakaavassa. Ylä: Schematic, distances to scale. In the top row four galaxies A, B, C and D in a line at equal spacing: B is at distance d from galaxy A, C at distance 2d and D at distance 3d. In the bottom row the same galaxies later, when all distances have grown by a factor of 1.5. At the bottom blue shift arrows: seen from galaxy A, B has moved by one, C by two and D by three units, so the shift and the speed v, 2v and 3v are directly proportional to the distance.
Aikajana, ei mittakaavassa: maailmankaik: Timeline, not to scale: the evolution of the universe from top to bottom. A vertical bar changes from red to blue as the universe cools. Time zero: the Big Bang, a hot and dense state. 3–20 minutes: the first nuclei, hydrogen and helium. 380 000 years: atoms form and the background radiation is released. About 200 million years: the first stars. 9.2 billion years: the Sun and the Earth form. 13.8 billion years: now, the temperature of the background radiation is 2.7 kelvins.
Aurinko ja Maa syntyvät: the Sun and the Earth form
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: ytimen sidosenerg: Graph to scale: the binding energy per nucleon of a nucleus in megaelectronvolts as a function of the mass number A, with A from zero to 250. The points are the values of 32 nuclei calculated from atomic masses, as in the chapter Mass defect and nuclear binding energy. The peak is at iron-56, about 8.8 MeV, and a vertical dashed line is drawn through it. To the left of the peak is an orange arrow: fusion in stars produces nuclei from helium to iron and releases energy. To the right of the peak is a grey arrow: nuclei heavier than iron form in neutron capture in supernovae and in neutron star collisions.
Kaavakuva, ei mittakaavassa: tähtien ja: Schematic, not to scale: the orbital speed v of stars and gas as a function of the distance r from the centre of the galaxy. Both curves rise near the centre. The grey dashed line is the speed that the gravity of the visible matter would explain: it decreases far from the centre. The blue solid curve with measurement points is the measured speed: it stays almost constant all the way to the outskirts of the galaxy. The difference points to invisible dark matter.
Vaakapalkki mittakaavassa: maailmankaikk: Horizontal bar to scale: the energy content of the universe based on the measurements of the Planck satellite. Ordinary matter, of which the stars, gas and we are made, is about 5 percent, dark matter about 26 percent and dark energy about 69 percent.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: galaksien etäänty: Graph to scale: the recession speed v of galaxies in kilometres per second as a function of the distance in megaparsecs, with the distance from zero to 300 megaparsecs and the speed from zero to 21 000 kilometres per second. The eight points are values of the model of the galaxies of the simulation; they are close to the line v = H0 d through the origin, whose slope is 70 kilometres per second per megaparsec. Dashed lines show a point read from the line: at a distance of 200 megaparsecs the speed is 14 000 kilometres per second.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: yhdeksän galaksin: Graph to scale: the recession speed v of nine galaxies in kilometres per second as a function of the distance in megaparsecs, with the distance from zero to 300 megaparsecs and the speed from zero to 21 000 kilometres per second, grid spacing 50 megaparsecs and 3000 kilometres per second. A line through the origin has been fitted to the points, and it passes through the grid point d = 250 Mpc, v = 18 000 km/s.
